name: Chang'e 4 (Yutu-2 rover and Queqiao-1 relay)
short_status: Landed Jan 3, 2019 in Von Kármán crater, first-ever far-side landing; lander and Yutu-2 last officially reported working in Sep 2024, Yutu-2 largely stationary since Mar 2024 with last official odometer 1,613 m (no later official status found as of Sep 28, 2026)
tagline: CNSA · China · Rover · 2019 · The robotic return Operating
stats: landing ever on the lunar far side
Yutu-2 odometer, longest-lived lunar rover (last official figure, Sep 2024)
on the far side; lander last officially reported working in Sep 2024
beyond the Moon: Queqiao-1 relay halo orbit at Earth-Moon L2

facts.label: Queqiao-1 relay launch
facts.value: 20 May 2018 UTC, Long March 4C from Xichang; 425 kg, 4.2 m relay dish

facts.label: Queqiao-1 mission orbit
facts.value: Earth-Moon L2 halo orbit, about 65,000 km beyond the Moon; entered 14 June 2018

facts.label: Chang'e 4 launch
facts.value: 7 December 2018, 18:23 UTC, Long March 3B from Xichang; total launch mass 3,780 kg

facts.label: Landing
facts.value: 3 January 2019, 02:26 UTC (10:26 Beijing time), floor of Von Kármán crater (186 km diameter), South Pole-Aitken basin

facts.label: Landing site coordinates
facts.value: 45.4561 S, 177.5885 E, elevation -5,927 m (LROC NAC stereo DTM)

facts.label: Site name
facts.value: Statio Tianhe, IAU-approved 15 February 2019, only the second "Statio" on the Moon after Apollo 11's Statio Tranquillitatis

facts.label: Yutu-2 rover
facts.value: 140 kg, solar powered, 3-month design life; deployed about 12 hours after landing; passed the Soviet Lunokhod 1 longevity record in late 2019

facts.label: Last official odometer
facts.value: 1,613 m, reported by Chinese media September 2024; no official update since

facts.label: LRO mobility analysis
facts.value: Motion slowed through 2023 and stopped in March 2024 per LRO image analysis by Phil Stooke (published 14 Jan 2025)

facts.label: First plant on the Moon
facts.value: Cotton seed sprouted in the Chongqing University mini-biosphere, announced 15 Jan 2019; the sprout froze during the first lunar night

facts.label: First far-side radiation measurement
facts.value: German LND instrument measured about 60 microsieverts per hour equivalent dose on the surface (Science Advances, 25 Sep 2020)

facts.label: Possible mantle material
facts.value: Yutu-2's VNIS spectrometer found olivine and low-calcium pyroxene consistent with excavated upper-mantle material (Li et al., Nature, May 2019)

facts.label: Relay handover
facts.value: Queqiao-1 exceeded its roughly 5-year design life; CNSA said Queqiao-2 (launched 20 Mar 2024) takes over Chang'e 4 relay services

facts.label: Companion microsats
facts.value: Longjiang-1 failed to reach lunar orbit; Longjiang-2 operated in lunar orbit until a deliberate impact on 31 July 2019

facts.label: International payloads
facts.value: LND dosimeter (Kiel University/DLR, Germany) on the lander, ASAN neutrals analyzer (Sweden) on Yutu-2, NCLE low-frequency radio experiment (Netherlands) on Queqiao-1

timeline: Queqiao-1 relay satellite launches on a Long March 4C from Xichang
Queqiao-1 enters its Earth-Moon L2 halo orbit, ready to relay far-side signals
Chang'e 4 launches at 18:23 UTC on a Long March 3B from Xichang
First-ever soft landing on the lunar far side at 02:26 UTC in Von Kármán crater; Yutu-2 rolls off about 12 hours later
China announces a cotton seed has sprouted on board, the first plant germinated on the Moon; it dies in the lunar night cold
30 Jan to 1 Feb 2019
NASA's LRO images the lander, then resolves both lander and rover from 82 km altitude
IAU names the landing site Statio Tianhe, with nearby craters Zhinyu, Hegu and Tianjin and peak Mons Tai
Nature paper reports VNIS detection of possible mantle-derived olivine and pyroxene in Von Kármán crater
Companion microsatellite Longjiang-2 ends its mission with a deliberate lunar impact
LND team publishes the first systematic radiation dose measurements from the lunar surface, about 60 microsieverts per hour
Mar 2024
Yutu-2 stops moving per later LRO image analysis; the same month Queqiao-2 launches to take over relay duties
Sep 2024
Last official odometer report: 1,613 m driven; Chinese media mark Yutu-2 as the world's longest-working lunar rover
SpaceNews reports LRO imagery shows no rover motion since March 2024, suggesting Yutu-2 can no longer drive
Unofficial analyses of 2025 LRO frames report small movements; CNSA has published no odometer update, so the rover's mobility remains unconfirmed (as of Sep 2026)
